name: Dr. M. I. Sahadulla
bio: Chairman and Managing Director, KIMSHealth – India and GCC. Senior Consultant in Internal Medicine and Lead Examiner and Organizer for PACES at Trivandrum and Examiner at other centers.

name: Dr. A. Saifudeen
org: KIMSHEALTH · Internal Medicine and Benign Haematology
qual: MBBS, MD, MRCP (UK), FRCP (London), FRCP (Glasgow), FRCP (Ireland), FRCP (Edinburgh) & FRSPH (London)
bio: Dr Saifudeen is a Senior Consultant in KIMSHealth in the Department of Internal Medicine and Benign Haematology, with over 45 years of experience in Clinical Medicine and 20 years of faculty experience with the Royal College of UK. He is also a veteran faculty and the Chief Organizer of the PACES examination at KIMSHealth, Trivandrum. He was previously employed at the Sultan Qaboos Hospital in Salalah under the Ministry of Health, Oman as the Head of the Department of Medicine, and Haematology for 32 years. Dr Saifudeen is a Postgraduate in Internal Medicine from the Madras University in Chennai, India. He completed his MD meritoriously as the best outgoing student in 1982, following which he worked as a specialist in Internal Medicine with the Kerala Health Services and in Saudi Arabia. He is also a member of the International Society of Haematology (ISH), the International Society of Thrombosis & Haemostatis and The American Society of Haematology. He has had 25 publications and presentations in various journals.

name: Dr. Prasad Nair
role: Senior Consultant Nephrologist and Transplant Physician
bio: Dr. Prasad Nair is a Senior Consultant in Nephrology and Transplant. He completed his undergraduate (MBBS) and postgraduate (MD, Gen Med) studies in India. He had his specialty training in Nephrology and transplant in the UK for 5 years and during that period he successfully obtained his MRCP UK in 1993. He was later awarded FRCP from the Royal Colleges of London and Ireland. Dr. Prasad took up his present job in the Ministry of Health, Kuwait in 1995 and is an undergraduate and postgraduate faculty and examiner in Kuwait. He has been an MRCP PACES examiner since 2008 and has examined in various PACES examination Centres in the Middle East and India. He has trained many candidates to succeed in the PACES examination in the past many years. Dr. Prasad is one of the founding members of Excelpaces.

name: Dr. Ajit Thomas
role: Consultant in Internal and Acute Medicine
org: KIMSHEALTH · Programme Director, Internal Medicine Training
qual: MD, MRCP(UK), MRCP(UK) Acute Medicine, FRCP(Lon)
bio: Consultant in Internal and Acute Medicine in KIMSHealth, and Programme Director for Internal Medicine Training (IMT) run in collaboration with RCP at Trivandrum. He is actively involved in organizing PACES exams in Trivandrum and is a PACES Examiner locally and in other Centres in India.

name: Dr. Donald L. Farquhar
qual: FRCP Edinburgh; International Medical Director, MRCP (UK), 2015–2023
bio: Dr Farquhar qualified from the University of Edinburgh in 1979 and subsequently trained in Edinburgh and Melbourne, Australia. He was a Consultant at the St John’s Hospital from 1990 until 2015 and was the Clinical Director for all Medicine services for 10 years. He has had 40 papers published in peer-reviewed journals. He has been an MRCP (UK) International Examiner for over 20 years. He has examined over 4500 PACES candidates. He was the International Medical Director (Assessment) for the Federation of Royal Colleges of Physicians from 2015 to 2023. He has opened 16 new MRCP PACES centers in countries including India, Pakistan, Myanmar, Malaysia, UAE, Kenya, Jamaica, and Sri Lanka. He has been involved in the MRCP teaching courses in Saudi Arabia, India, Pakistan, Myanmar, and Hong Kong. He has been an external examiner for the Singapore MMed, Bangladesh College of Physicians and Surgeons and Sri Lanka MMed and the Libya Medical Board.

name: Dr. Jacqueline Taylor
qual: MB ChB FRCP (Glasgow), Hon FRCPI, Hon FFPHM, DSc, Hon FCSSL, Hon FRCS (Eng), Hon FRCS (Edin), Hon FRCP (London), Fellow BSH
bio: Professor Jackie Taylor graduated from the University of Glasgow Medical School, trained, and dually accredited in General Internal Medicine and Geriatric Medicine, and was appointed to Glasgow Royal Infirmary. She has a sub-specialty interest in heart failure. She previously chaired the Heart Failure sub-group of the Cardiac Managed Clinical Network, responsible for the strategic development and delivery of multidisciplinary heart failure services. From a managerial perspective, she has been the Clinical Director, Associate Medical Director, and Clinical Quality Lead for Geriatric Medicine.

Professor Taylor has a major interest in the training and education of healthcare professionals. She is an Honorary Senior Clinical Lecturer and was made an Honorary Professor at the University of Glasgow in 2018. She is a past Chair of the British Geriatrics Society Cardiovascular Section. Professor Taylor’s other main professional roles have been as Honorary Secretary, Vice President, and President of the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Glasgow. She was the first woman ever to be elected to the role. As PRCPSG, she led the College through the COVID-19 pandemic. In recognition of her contribution to medicine, she has been awarded several Honorary Fellowships of Royal Colleges, an Honorary Doctorate of Science, and an MBE in the King’s New Year’s Honours list. She is currently the Associate Medical Director for the NHS Scotland Academy.

name: Dr. Eric Livingston
bio: Eric Livingston graduated from the University of Aberdeen Medical School in 1997 and trained in Respiratory Medicine in the West of Scotland. He obtained his MD from University of Glasgow in 2005. He is a Consultant Respiratory Physician at Glasgow Royal Infirmary, specialising in Sleep Disorders.

He is heavily involved in medical education, being a Training Programme Director for Respiratory Medicine, and a Foundation Programme Director in the West Region of the Scotland Deanery. He was Deputy Director of Medical Education at the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Glasgow. He is the College examiner representative on the Clinical Examining Board for MRCP UK and is an active host and PACES examiner.
He is Vice President (Medical) at the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Glasgow.

name: Dr. Elizabeth A. Murphy
org: University Hospital Wishaw · NHS Education Scotland
qual: MRCP (UK) 1989, MSc (Distinction) Clinical Leadership 2010, University of Glasgow School of Business
bio: Consultant Rheumatologist, University Hospital, Wishaw, and Associate Postgraduate Dean, NHS Education Scotland.

An examiner for the MRCP (UK) postgraduate examination in the UK and overseas, and chaired the Scenario Editorial Committee 2015-21. She was Director of Medical Education at the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Glasgow 2019-2023 and is currently Honorary Librarian for the College.
Previous President of the Scottish Society for Rheumatology and currently a trustee of The British Society for Rheumatology.

name: Dr. Manoj Pazhampallil Mathews
qual: MD, MRCP (UK), MRCP (Endocrinology & Diabetes), M.Sc (Diabetes), PGDD (Endocrinology & Diabetes), Cardiff, UK, FRCP (London), FRCP (Edinburgh), FRCPSG (Glasgow)
bio: Dr Manoj P. Mathews is a Senior Consultant in Internal Medicine. He completed his under graduation (MBBS) from Trivandrum Medical College followed by MD (Internal Medicine) from Lok Manya Tilak Government Medical College, Mumbai. He went to complete his MRCP (UK) followed by Speciality Certification (MRCP) in Endocrinology and Diabetes. He also completed a Post Graduate Diploma in Endocrinology and Diabetes followed by an M.Sc in Diabetes, both from Cardiff University, UK. He attained Fellowship of the Royal Colleges of London, Glasgow and Edinburgh. He has more than 27 years of clinical experience in Internal Medicine.

He was an Assistant Professor in Internal Medicine in India before continuing his teaching and academic duties in the UAE where he worked as Senior Internist/ Hospitalist and Unit Chief in Dubai Hospital and Adjunct Clinical Faculty in Dubai Medical College under the Dubai Health Authority. He has been actively involved in undergraduate and postgraduate teaching and examinations and has been a PACES Examiner at several centers in the UAE and India.

name: Dr. Shaji Mohamed Haneef
bio: Dr Shaji is a Senior Consultant in Kimshealth, Trivandrum in the department of Internal Medicine.

He has completed MBBS and MD (Medicine) from India and obtained MRCP(UK) in 2001 and FRCP(Edin) in 2016. Prior to joining Kimshealth he has worked in UAE for more than 25 years and has vast experience in teaching as a faculty of Dubai Medical College. He is also a MRCP PACES examiner and involved in teaching IMT students in Kimshealth.

name: Prof. Mathew Thomas
org: KIMSHEALTH Trivandrum and CSI Medical College
qual: MD, FRCP (London), FRCP (Edin), FICP, FISHTM – India
bio: Professor of Medicine and Hematology in KIMSHealth Trivandrum and CSI Medical College. He is actively involved with all MRCP PACES-related matters in Trivandrum and is a PACES examiner locally and in other Centres in India.

name: Dr. Venkat Mahadevan
role: Consultant Physician in General and Respiratory Medicine
bio: Dr. Mahadevan is the lead Consultant for Lung Cancer, Sleep disorders & Non-Invasive Ventilation at the James Paget University Hospital, Norfolk, UK. After Primary medical qualification from Madurai Kamaraj University in South India, Dr. Mahadevan got trained in General Medicine at the Madras Medical College. He has been in the UK since 1992, where he underwent higher training in General & Respiratory Medicine at Manchester & the Royal Brompton Hospital in London. He is a fellow of the Royal College of Physicians of London & Edinburgh, as well as the American College of Chest Physicians. He has been a Consultant Physician in the NHS over the past 2 decades. He is deeply involved in medical education with the teaching & training of medical students, junior doctors, and allied healthcare professionals. He is the Respiratory Module lead & Honorary Professor of Respiratory Medicine at Norwich Medical School & University of East Anglia.

Dr. Mahadevan has been a past editor of the RCP London Newsletter & the College Commentary. He has also previously served on RCP (London) Council. He is an MRCP (UK) examiner since 2005 & is Chair of the PACES Scenario Editorial Committee (SEC). He is also a core member of the RCP’s Clinical Examinations Board (CEB) & is the Chair of examiners at MRCP PACES diets both in the UK & overseas. He is one of the founder faculty members of the Excelpaces course at KIMSHealth.

name: Prof. Panduka Karunanayake
qual: MBBS (North Colombo), MD (Colombo), FRCP (London), Postgrad Cert Teach Higher Educ, Postgrad Dip ApplSociol (Colombo)
bio: Prof. Karunanayake is a Professor in Clinical Medicine in the Faculty of Medicine, University of Colombo, Sri Lanka. He is an Examiner in the MRCP (UK) PACES Examination, as well as in the MD Medicine Examination of the University of Colombo where he had also been a Chief Examiner. He is a Former Secretary of the Board of Study in Medicine, Postgraduate Institute of Medicine, University of Colombo; Past President of the Ceylon College of Physicians; and Past Vice-President of the Sri Lanka Medical Association. Professor Karunanayake’s area of research interest in clinical medicine is infectious disease, where he has published papers on dengue, leptospirosis and visceral leishmaniasis. He also has an abiding interest in Higher Education Pedagogy, Medical Social Sciences and Medical Humanities.

name: Prof. Sunil Bhandari
role: Consultant in Nephrology and Honorary Clinical Professor
org: Hull University Teaching Hospitals · Vice President, RCP Edinburgh
qual: MBChB, MRCP (UK), FRCP (Edin), PhD, M Clin Edu, FHEA, FASN
bio: Prof. Bhandari graduated from the University of Edinburgh, trained in Renal and Transplant Medicine in Yorkshire (UK) and Sydney Australia.

He is a Consultant in Nephrology and Honorary Professor at Hull York Medical School (HYMS) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust and Vice President for Royal College of Physicians Edinburgh (RCPE) and Deputy Head of School in Medicine for NHS England, Yorkshire and Humber.

He is a teacher – undergraduate, postgraduate and international. In addition, as Deputy Head of School he covers over 5000 trainees in the region and the Educational and Clinical Supervisors and Training Program Directors in the Medical Specialties. He is also a researcher aiming to answer important questions to improve patient outcomes, in particular delaying kidney progression, and a clinician caring for patients with kidney disease and kidney transplants.
